events.text: In 2024, Thai Oil reported Scope 1 emissions of 3,447,284,000 kg CO2e and Scope 2 emissions of 30,753,000 kg CO2e.

Thai Oil recruited and nominated Lieutenant General Apichat Chaiyadar to the Audit Committee and the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, Mr. Distat Hotrakitya to the Corporate Governance and Sustainability Committee, and Police Captain Piya Raksakul to the Audit Committee and the Corporate Governance and Sustainability Committee.

Thai Oil recruited and nominated Ms. Pattaralada Sa-ngasang as chairman of the Risk Management Committee, Ms. Peangpanor Boonklum to the Risk Management Committee, ending the office of the Corporate Governance and Sustainability Committee, and Mr. Chadil Chavanalikikorn to the Corporate Governance and Sustainability Committee.

Greenpeace Thailand issued a statement on June 6, 2025, urging Thai Oil Public Company Limited to take full responsibility for an oil spill that occurred at SBM-2, a mooring buoy off the coast of Sriracha, Chonburi, on June 5 around 11:54 PM.

Greenpeace Thailand demanded full responsibility from Thai Oil for the crude oil spill at SBM-2 operated by Thai Oil Public Company Limited in the open sea off Si Racha, and urged the government to take further action to prevent environmental harm, per its 7 June 2025 statement.

Samsung E&A (Thailand) Co., Ltd., Saipem Singapore Pte. Ltd., Petrofac South East Asia Pte. Ltd. and PSS Netherlands B.V. v. Thai Oil Public Company Limited — disclosure of Thai Oil Public Company Limited on arbitration proceedings relating to the Clean Fuel Project, Wednesday 26th March 2025.
